st: Toss the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper, chili powder and oil. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, fresh chile, lemon juice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt for the relish.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan to high heat. Thread the beef onto skewers if you like.
Grill the meat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Rest the meat for 3 minutes, then cut into smaller pieces.
Serve hot with the fresh tomato relish and a pinch of extra salt and chili for dipping.
Season the beef with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef in batches for 8 minutes per batch. Move to a plate.
Cook the onions for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the beef back with the tomatoes, bay leaves and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 1 hour 15 minutes without stirring much, as in a traditional potjie.
Layer the carrots on top, then the potatoes. Cover and cook another 45 minutes.
Check that the beef and vegetables are very tender. Taste and add salt. Serve with rice or bread.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the beef for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 cup]] water. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
Bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil with [[0.5 tsp]] salt in another pot.
Mix [[1 cup]] of the millet flour with [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth. Stir it into the boiling water.
Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Add the rest of the flour, a handful at a time, and press the porridge against the pot with a wooden spoon until very stiff and smooth.
Cover and cook on low for 5 minutes.
Shape into balls and serve with the beef stew.
Mix the garlic, oil, salt, pepper and coriander. Rub over the steaks and lamb, then rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Light charcoal or wood and let it burn until covered with gray ash, about 30 minutes.
Brush the grate clean and oil lightly.
Grill the sausage first, for 15 minutes, turning, until cooked to 160°F (71°C).
Grill the lamb for 4 to 5 minutes per side, and the steaks for 3 to 5 minutes per side to your liking.
Add the onion wedges to the grill and cook for 8 minutes until charred.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes before serving with pap or bread.
Toast the coriander seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind them.
Keep the ground meats very cold. Mix in the coriander, cloves, nutmeg, pepper, [[1.5 tbsp]] salt, vinegar and Worcestershire in a large bowl.
Mix gently with your hands for 2 minutes until just combined.
Fry a small patty to taste, then adjust the seasoning.
Rinse the casings and slide them onto the sausage stuffer tube.
Fill the casings with the mixture, without trapping air, then coil it into a spiral. Prick any air bubbles.
Rest the sausage in the fridge for 1 hour so the flavors blend.
Cook over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, to an internal 160°F (71°C).

ing: in thick strips, cut with the grain
st: Trim the beef of most surface fat and slice into strips about 1 inch thick and 8 inches long, cutting with the grain.
Lay the strips in a glass dish and pour over the vinegar. Turn to coat and leave for 30 minutes.
Toast the coriander seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then crush them coarsely. Mix with the salt, pepper and brown sugar.
Drain the beef and pat with towels. Rub the spice mix all over the strips, then layer in the dish and cover.
Refrigerate overnight, turning once.
Brush off the extra spices. Hang the strips on hooks in a well-ventilated dry spot, or in a dehydrator or cool oven with the door ajar, at about 90°F (32°C).
Dry for 3 to 5 days, turning, until firm but a little pliable. Slice thin to serve. Keep refrigerated.

ing: for frying, plus 1 tbsp in the dough
st: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add [[1 tbsp]] oil and the warm water and mix to a soft, sticky dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Cook the onion in a pan with a little oil for 4 minutes. Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully browned to 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the curry powder, tomato paste and a splash of water. Simmer for 10 minutes and season with salt.
Punch down the dough and shape into golf-ball-size rounds. Rest for 15 minutes.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a pot to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the dough balls for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked inside.
Drain, split open and fill with the mince.
Soak the dried worms in warm water for 30 minutes to rehydrate. Drain and rinse.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chile for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until saucy.
Add the worms and [[2 cups]] water. Bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered on medium-low for 15 minutes until tender and the liquid is mostly reduced.
Season with salt and serve with pap or rice.
